## Dormant Codex source adaptation

This adapter is available for source review only. It is not indexed, installed, scheduled, or activated. Existing operator exclusion remains in force. Reading this file grants no provider use, credentials, external posting, webhook exposure or automation execution. Resolve every required tool against the actual native host. Preserve the named upstream product; a local fixture proves only its stated boundary.

# Set up Benny on Codex

1. Read the complete preserved Benny pack at `sources/cursor-plugins/upstream-tree/pstack/automations/benny/`, including FOR_AGENTS.md, both operational skills, templates and references. Copy or merge the pack into a caller-approved source directory only when that setup is authorized; preserve destination-only files and user-owned configuration.
2. Resolve shared `cursor-how`, `cursor-why`, `cursor-tdd`, `cursor-unslop` and the named `cursor-principle-*` leaves through native skill discovery. Do not write Cursor settings or claim project activation from source availability. Verify a fresh target session separately.
3. Fill the existing configuration template, feature map and optional routing map outside the managed pack. Preserve every required source channel, triage identity, repository, tracker, control adapter, feature map, status marker, model and budget field. Use the native model inventory and operator policy. Keep secrets outside committed files.
4. Verify authorized Slack thread reads/replies, attachment access, tracker search/create/update/compensation, repository history, draft-PR creation and the configured app-control adapter. Native tools must expose actual required schemas. Never invent backend endpoints or substitute a root-channel post.
5. Verify all seven app-control capabilities in the upstream control-adapter reference, including real UI driving, screenshots, recording and cleanup. Keep repro disabled if any is absent.
6. Inspect existing native automations before creating duplicates. Codex scheduling tools can implement an explicitly requested recurring check or continuation. They do not by themselves provide the upstream new-Slack-message event trigger. If that trigger is unavailable, report it and leave event-driven activation incomplete; do not silently convert it to polling. A polling adaptation requires the operator to select that change.
7. Prepare separate triage and repro prompts pointing at their stable, reviewed source paths and secret-free configuration. Use the actual native automation authoring interface only after activation is authorized. Do not use Cursor's automate editor, protocol links, settings, or hidden backend.
8. Run the upstream thread-safety test on a designated test event after authorized setup: immutable parent coordinates, trusted marker author, exactly one triage verdict, no source root post, verified tracker compensation, no worker Slack write capabilities. The existing `scripts/cursor_benny_adapters.py` proves local event/marker gates only; it does not prove live Slack, tracker, scheduler, or UI execution.
9. Report copied source/configuration, dependency and trigger gaps, fresh-session proof, thread-safety evidence and activation state separately. Do not claim Benny running from a fixture.
